Quick steps that each ring for two beats.

```tine
voice bells = [c5 e5 g5 c6].fast(2).dur(2).inst(bell).vel(.5)
```

Fixed short notes, whatever the step length.

```tine
voice line = [c4:3 e4 g4:2 c5:2].dur(1/4).inst(pluck)
```

See also: [legato](#legato).

### set

`set(p, name, value)`: Attach any named parameter to events (it is passed through to MIDI CC maps and exports).

`set(name, value)` attaches any named setting to notes. Tine passes it on to MIDI control maps and exports, so it can carry settings for other software.

A custom setting, readable by anything that consumes the notes.

```tine
voice lead = [c4 e4 g4].set("brightness", .7).inst(keys)
```

A setting with a pattern of values, one per note.

```tine
voice hats = [hat*4].set("variation", [0 1 2 3])
```

See also: [ctl](#ctl).

### inst

`inst(p, name, ...options)`: Choose a built-in instrument: keys, sine, tri, saw, square, pluck, bass, pad, bell, organ, kit, or a loaded sample name.

`inst(name)` picks a built-in instrument: keys, pluck, bass, pad, bell, organ, lead, upright, vibes, sine, saw and more, the synth presets (supersaw, tb303, reese, wobble, chip, brass, strings, marimba), or a loaded sample. Named options set the instrument's settings in one go.

The same line on three instruments, one per bar.

```tine
let line = [c4 e4 g4 e4]
voice tune = cat(line.inst(keys), line.inst(pluck), line.inst(bell))
```

Layer one line on two instruments, in different octaves, for a new combined color.

```tine
let line = [c4 e4 g4 e4 a4 g4 e4 d4]
voice both = stack(line.octave(-1).inst(upright), line.octave(1).inst(vibes).vel(.4))
```

Options after the name set its settings: here a synth preset with its filter changed.

```tine
voice acid = [a1 a1 a2 a1 c2 a1 g2 a1].inst(tb303, res: .6, cutoff: 600)
```

See also: [sample](#sample), [wave](#wave), [gm](#gm).

### sample

`sample(p, name, n: 0, fit: false)`: Play a sound from the sample library: a full name ("bd_haus"), a bank ("bd", with n choosing among its sounds), or "bank:n". On a drum phrase with no name it plays the bundled kit. name and n may be patterns. With fit: true the sound is stretched to the note's length.

`sample(name, n)` plays notes on a sound from the sample library. Give a full name ("bd_haus"), a bank ("bd", with n picking among its sounds), or "bank:n". On drum names with no name it plays the bundled kit. Pitched notes play the sample higher or lower: c4 is as recorded.

Drum names through the bundled kit.

```tine
voice kit = [kick . snare . kick kick snare .].sample()
```

A bank, with a pattern choosing which of its sounds plays.

```tine
voice hats = [x*8].sample("hat", n: [0 3 5 7])
```

A pitched sample: notes play it at their pitch, and [`cut`](#cut) stops each note when the next starts.

```tine
voice bass = [c4 . eb4 g4].sample("bass_voxy_c").cut(1)
```

See also: [inst](#inst), [begin](#begin), [loopAt](#loopat), [samples](#samples).

### begin

`begin(p, x)`: Start playing a sample from this point, 0 (its start) to 1 (its end).

`begin(x)` starts a sample partway through, from 0 (its start) to 1 (its end).

Skip the first half of a loop.

```tine
voice loop = ["loop_amen"].begin(.5)
```

A pattern of start points makes a chopped-up rhythm from one sound.

```tine
voice cut = ["loop_amen"*8].begin([0 .25 .5 .125 0 .75 .5 .25]).end([.125 .375 .625 .25 .125 .875 .625 .375])
```

See also: [end](#end), [slice](#slice), [chop](#chop).

### end

`end(p, x)`: Stop playing a sample at this point, 0 to 1.

`end(x)` stops a sample at a point from 0 to 1. With [`begin`](#begin), it picks out a piece.

Only the first tenth of a long sound: a short stab.

```tine
voice stab = ["ambi_choir" . . "ambi_choir"].end(.1)
```

A pattern of end points: hits that get longer.

```tine
voice drum = ["loop_amen"*4].end([.05 .1 .2 .3])
```

See also: [begin](#begin), [slice](#slice).

### speed

`speed(p, x)`: Sample playback rate: 2 is an octave up and twice as fast, -1 plays it backwards.

`speed(x)` sets a sample's playback rate. 2 is an octave up and twice as fast, 0.5 an octave down, and a negative speed plays it backwards.

A loop played backwards.

```tine
voice back = ["loop_amen"].loopAt(2).speed(-1)
```

A pattern of speeds: the same hit at different pitches.

```tine
voice perc = ["perc_bell"*4].speed([1 1.5 2 .75])
```

See also: [accel](#accel), [loopAt](#loopat).

### accel

`accel(p, x)`: Change a sample's speed by x every second while it plays: speed(1).accel(-1) is a tape stop.

`accel(x)` changes a sample's speed by x every second while it plays. [`speed(1).accel(-1)`](#speed) slows to a stop, like a tape machine switched off.

A tape stop.

```tine
voice stop = ["loop_amen"].speed(1).accel(-1)
```

A rising sweep from one sound.

```tine
voice rise = ["ambi_drone"].speed(.5).accel(.5)
```

See also: [speed](#speed).

### cut

`cut(p, group)`: Cut group: a sample in this group stops the one before it, in any voice. Choke an open hat with a closed one.

`cut(group)` puts samples in a cut group: a new sound in the group stops the one before it, in any voice. Use it to choke an open hat with a closed one.

The open hat is cut off by the next closed hat.

```tine
voice closed = [hat . hat . hat . hat .].sample().cut(1)
voice open   = [. ohat . . . ohat . .].sample().cut(1)
```

A long pitched sample cut by each new note, so it plays like a monophonic synth.

```tine
voice bass = [c4 c4 eb4 . g4 f4 . c4].sample("bass_voxy_c").cut(1)
```

See also: [sample](#sample), [legato](#legato).

### loopAt

`loopAt(p, bars)`: Make a sample last this many bars, whatever the tempo: the phrase is slowed to that length and the sample stretched to fit. Add chop to keep a long loop in time: ["loop_amen"].loopAt(2).chop(16).

`loopAt(bars)` makes a sample last this many bars, whatever the tempo. Add [`chop`](#chop) so a long loop stays in time as it plays.

The amen break, stretched to two bars and chopped so it follows the tempo.

```tine
tempo 140
voice amen = ["loop_amen"].loopAt(2).chop(16)
```

Change the tempo and the loop follows.

```tine
tempo 90
voice loop = ["loop_breakbeat"].loopAt(2).chop(8)
voice bass = [c2 . . c2 . . eb2 .].inst(bass)
```

See also: [chop](#chop), [splice](#splice), [speed](#speed).

### slice

`slice(p, n, i)`: Cut the sample into n equal pieces and play piece i (from 0). i may be a pattern: .slice(8, [0 3 2 7]).

`slice(n, i)` cuts a sample into n equal pieces and plays piece i (from 0). With a pattern for i, it rearranges a loop.

A break cut into eight and played in a new order.

```tine
voice beat = ["loop_amen"*8].slice(8, [0 1 0 3 4 7 6 2])
```

Random slices each step, seeded.

```tine
seed 5
voice glitch = ["loop_amen"*16].slice(16, dice(run(16), 16))
```

See also: [splice](#splice), [chop](#chop), [begin](#begin).

### splice

`splice(p, n, i)`: Like slice, but each piece is stretched to fill its note, so a sliced loop stays in tempo.

`splice(n, i)` is like [`slice`](#slice), but each piece is stretched to fill its note, so a sliced loop stays in tempo at any speed.

A spliced break: slices fit their steps exactly.

```tine
voice beat = ["loop_amen"*8].splice(8, [0 1 2 3 0 5 6 6])
```

Doubling the steps doubles the slicing; each piece is squeezed to fit.

```tine
voice fast = ["loop_amen"*16].splice(8, run(16))
```

See also: [slice](#slice), [loopAt](#loopat).

### chop

`chop(p, n)`: Split each note into n notes that play successive parts of its sample. With loopAt, a loop follows the tempo: loop_amen.loopAt(2).chop(16).

`chop(n)` splits each note into n notes that play successive parts of its sample. With [`loopAt`](#loopat), a long loop follows the tempo; with other functions, it lets you treat each piece separately.

A loop chopped into sixteen and stretched over two bars.

```tine
voice amen = ["loop_amen"].loopAt(2).chop(16)
```

Chop, then rearrange the pieces with [`rev`](#rev).

```tine
voice back = ["loop_amen"].loopAt(1).chop(8).rev
```

Chop, then thin out the pieces at random.

```tine
seed 4
voice gaps = ["loop_breakbeat"].loopAt(2).chop(16).degrade(.3)
```

See also: [loopAt](#loopat), [slice](#slice), [ply](#ply).

### gm

`gm(p, program, bank: 0)`: Play notes on an instrument of the loaded SoundFont: a General MIDI program number from 1 (piano) to 128, or a name to search for, .gm("violin"). On drum names with no program it plays the drum kit.

`gm(program)` plays notes on an instrument from a loaded SoundFont: a General MIDI program number from 1 (piano) to 128, or a name to search for. On drum names with no program it plays the bank's drum kit. It needs a [`soundfont(...)`](#soundfont) line.

Piano, violin and drums from a General MIDI bank. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
soundfont("github:mrbumpy409/GeneralUser-GS/GeneralUser-GS.sf2")
voice piano = <c4@maj a3@m f3@maj g3@maj>.gm(1)
voice tune  = [e5 . d5 c5 . . g4 .].gm("violin")
voice drums = [kick hat snare hat].gm()
```

A pattern of programs: the same line on different instruments. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
soundfont("github:mrbumpy409/GeneralUser-GS/GeneralUser-GS.sf2")
voice tune = [c4 e4 g4 c5].gm(<1 12 25 74>)
```

See also: [soundfont](#soundfont), [inst](#inst).

### dirt

`dirt(p, sound: "", orbit: 0)`: Send to SuperDirt (TidalCycles' sound engine) instead of the built-in sound, over OSC from tine daw or tine dirt. sound is a SuperDirt sample bank or synth; without it, sample names, drum names and instruments are translated.

`dirt(sound, orbit)` sends a voice to SuperDirt, TidalCycles' sound engine, over OSC, from `tine daw` or `tine dirt`. Without a sound, sample names, drum names and instruments are translated.

Drums on SuperDirt's own samples. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
voice drums = [kick . snare .].dirt()
```

A SuperDirt synth for the melody, on its own orbit for separate effects. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
voice lead = [c4 e4 g4 b4].dirt("superpiano", orbit: 1)
```

See also: [midi](#midi).

### midi

`midi(p, channel: 1, port: "")`: Send to an external MIDI device instead of the built-in synth.

`midi(channel, port)` sends a voice to an external MIDI device instead of the built-in sound. In the DAW, open the MIDI tab and enable MIDI first.

A bass line to a synth on channel 1. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
voice bass = [c2 . c2 eb2 . g2 . .].midi(1)
```

Drums to a drum machine on channel 10, the General MIDI drum channel. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
voice drums = {[kick*4] [. clap . clap] [. hat]*4}.midi(10)
```

Choose the output port by name when several devices are connected. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
voice pad = <c3@maj7 f3@maj7>.slow(2).midi(2, port: "IAC")
```

See also: [ctl](#ctl), [program](#program), [mpe](#mpe), [as_cc](#as_cc).

### ctl

`ctl(p, number, value)`: Send a MIDI control change (value 0 to 1) just before each note. value may be a pattern or signal: .ctl(74, sine(4)).

`ctl(number, value)` sends a MIDI control change, from 0 to 1, just before each note. The value can be a pattern or a signal, to move a knob on your synth in time.

Sweep a synth's filter (CC 74) with a sine. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
voice bass = [c2*8].midi(1).ctl(74, sine(4))
```

A pattern of values, one per note. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
voice lead = [c4 e4 g4 c5].midi(1).ctl(71, [0 .3 .6 1])
```

See also: [as_cc](#as_cc), [midi](#midi), [cc](#cc).

### program

`program(p, n)`: Choose an instrument on external gear with a MIDI program change (1 to 128, as printed in General MIDI lists). It is sent only when it changes.

`program(n)` chooses an instrument on external gear with a MIDI program change, 1 to 128 as General MIDI lists number them. It is sent only when it changes.

Piano on channel 1. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
voice keys = [c4@maj7 . a3@m7 .].midi(1).program(1)
```

Switch instruments each bar with a pattern. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
voice tune = [c4 e4 g4 c5].midi(1).program(<1 25 41>)
```

See also: [midi](#midi), [gm](#gm).

### as_cc

`as_cc(p, number, rate: 16)`: Turn a voice of numbers (0 to 1) into MIDI control changes instead of notes: voice sweep = sine(4).as_cc(74).midi(1). A signal is sampled `rate` times per bar.

`as_cc(number, rate)` turns a voice of numbers from 0 to 1 into MIDI control changes instead of notes. A signal is sampled `rate` times per bar. It is automation as its own voice.

A slow filter sweep as its own voice. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
voice sweep = sine(4).as_cc(74).midi(1)
voice bass  = [c2*8].midi(1)
```

A stepped pattern of values, sent as CC 1 (the mod wheel). *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
voice mod = [0 .25 .5 1].as_cc(1).midi(1)
```

See also: [ctl](#ctl), [cc](#cc).

### mpe

`mpe(p)`: Send each note on its own MIDI channel (2 to 16) so microtonal pitch bends do not collide.

`mpe` sends each note on its own MIDI channel (2 to 16), so microtonal pitch bends do not collide. Use it with an MPE synth.

Chords tuned a little sharp, each note bent on its own channel. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
voice pad = <^1@9 ^6@7>.slow(2).transpose(.14).midi(1).mpe
```

A 31-tone line with chords, sent to an MPE synth. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
key c edo(31, [0 5 10 13 18 23 28])
voice keys = <^1@7 ^4@7 ^5@7>.midi(1).mpe
```

See also: [midi](#midi), [edo](#edo).

## Input

### soundfont

`soundfont(source)`: Load a SoundFont 2 (.sf2) bank, as a top-level line: a file next to the piece, a URL, or "github:user/repo/path.sf2". Then play its instruments with .gm(). General MIDI banks such as GeneralUser GS give all 128 standard instruments and the drum kits.

`soundfont(source)` loads a SoundFont 2 (.sf2) bank, as a line of its own: a file next to the piece, a URL, or "github:user/repo/path.sf2". Then [`.gm()`](#gm) plays its instruments. Only the first such line is used.

Load a free General MIDI bank from GitHub and play a piano. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
soundfont("github:mrbumpy409/GeneralUser-GS/GeneralUser-GS.sf2")
voice piano = <c4@maj a3@m f3@maj g3@maj>.gm(1)
```

A file next to the piece works the same way. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
soundfont("GeneralUser-GS.sf2")
voice strings = <c3@maj7 f3@maj7>.gm("strings")
```

See also: [gm](#gm), [samples](#samples).

### samples

`samples(source)`: Load a sample pack, as a top-level line: a folder (command line), a URL of a strudel.json sample map, or "github:user/repo" for that repository's strudel.json. Sounds load on first use.

`samples(source)` loads a sample pack, as a line of its own: a folder (from the command line), the URL of a strudel.json sample map, or "github:user/repo" for that repository's map. Sounds download the first time they play.

Load the TidalCycles sample set and play its banks. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
samples("github:tidalcycles/dirt-samples")
voice beat = ["bd" "hh" "sn" "hh"]
```

A pack's banks replace bundled banks of the same name; pick sounds with n. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
samples("github:tidalcycles/dirt-samples")
voice hats = [x*8].sample("hh", n: [0 1 2 3])
```

See also: [sample](#sample), [soundfont](#soundfont).

### cc

`cc(number, channel: any)`: A live signal (0 to 1) from a MIDI controller knob or fader.

`cc(number, channel)` is a live signal, 0 to 1, from a knob or fader on a MIDI controller. Use it anywhere a number goes, through [`range`](#range). With no controller connected it reads 0.

Knob 74 opens the filter. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
voice acid = [^1 ^1 ^8 ^1 ^b3 ^1 ^5 ^b7].fast(2).octave(-2).inst(saw).cutoff(cc(74).range(200, 5000)).res(.7)
```

A fader controls how much of a part plays. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
voice hats = [hat*16].degrade(cc(71))
```

See also: [held](#held), [ctl](#ctl).

### held

`held(steps: 1)`: The notes currently held on your MIDI keyboard, as a chord, sampled `steps` times per bar. Try held(4).arp.

`held(steps)` is the chord you are holding on a MIDI keyboard, sampled `steps` times per bar. Follow it with [`arp`](#arp) and you have an arpeggiator. With nothing held it is silent.

An arpeggiator: whatever you hold, in sixteenths, up and down. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
voice hands = held(16).arp("updown").inst(pluck).vel(.6)
```

Your chord, strummed on each beat, with a bass from its root. *(Needs a file, a device or the network to be heard.)*

```tine device
voice chords = held(4).strum.inst(keys)
voice bass   = held(4).root.octave(-2).inst(bass)
```

See also: [cc](#cc), [arp](#arp).

## Generators

### sine

`sine(period: 1)`: A smooth signal from 0 to 1 and back, once per `period` bars.

`sine(period)` is a smooth signal that rises from 0 to 1 and falls back once every `period` bars. Signals are continuous: each note reads the value at the moment it plays. Rescale with [`range`](#range), then use it wherever a number goes.

A filter that opens and closes over eight bars.

```tine
voice bass = [c2 c2 c3 c2 eb2 c2 g2 bb1].fast(2).inst(saw).cutoff(sine(8).range(300, 3000))
```

Velocity from a one-bar sine: the line swells in the middle of each bar.

```tine
voice hats = [hat*16].vel(sine(1).range(.2, .9))
```

Pan a part slowly from side to side.

```tine
voice keys = [c4@maj7 . e4@m7 .].inst(keys).pan(sine(4).range(-.8, .8))
```

See also: [tri](#tri), [saw](#saw), [range](#range), [seg](#seg).

### tri

`tri(period: 1)`: A triangle signal, 0 up to 1 and back.

`tri(period)` rises in a straight line from 0 to 1 and falls back, once every `period` bars. It sounds more even than [`sine`](#sine), which lingers at the top and bottom.

A steady sweep of the cutoff, up for two bars and down for two.

```tine
voice acid = [a1 a1 a2 a1 c2 a1 g2 a1].inst(tb303).cutoff(tri(4).range(400, 2400))
```

Turned into notes with [`seg`](#seg) and [`range`](#range), it plays a scale up and down.

```tine
voice run = tri(1).seg(16).range(0, 7).map(x => round(x)).degrees.inst(pluck)
```

See also: [sine](#sine), [saw](#saw), [seg](#seg).

### saw

`saw(period: 1)`: A ramp from 0 to 1 every `period` bars.

`saw(period)` ramps from 0 up to 1 every `period` bars, then jumps back. Use it for builds that start again, like a riser before each section.

A crescendo over each bar, then back to quiet.

```tine
voice snare = [snare*16].vel(saw(1).range(.1, 1))
```

A filter that opens over four bars and snaps shut, a classic build.

```tine
voice pad = <c3@m7 ab2@maj7>.inst(supersaw).lpf(saw(4).range(200, 6000))
```

Velocity from a three-bar ramp on a seven-step pattern: the accent moves as the two cycles drift apart.

```tine
voice swirl = [hat*7].vel(saw(3).range(.2, .8))
```

See also: [sine](#sine), [tri](#tri), [range](#range).

### square

`square(period: 1)`: Alternates between 0 and 1.

`square(period)` alternates between 0 and 1, holding each for half the period. It switches a setting between two values.

Two velocities, alternating each half bar.

```tine
voice hats = [hat*8].vel(square(1).range(.3, .9))
```

Pan a part hard left for one bar, hard right for the next.

```tine
voice keys = [c4 e4 g4 e4].inst(keys).pan(square(2).range(-1, 1))
```

See also: [sine](#sine), [range](#range).

### noise

`noise(rate: 16)`: A seeded random signal holding a new value `rate` times per bar.

`noise(rate)` is a random signal that holds a new value `rate` times per bar. It is seeded, so it replays exactly.

Random velocity for every hat.

```tine
seed 1
voice hats = [hat*16].vel(noise(16).range(.1, .6))
```

A random cutoff that changes every beat, for a restless bass.

```tine
seed 1
voice bass = [c2*8].inst(saw).cutoff(noise(4).range(300, 2500)).res(.5)
```

See also: [drift](#drift), [rand](#rand).

### drift

`drift(rate: 1)`: A smooth seeded random signal, wandering between 0 and 1.

`drift(rate)` is a smooth random signal that wanders between 0 and 1. It moves about `rate` times per bar. Use it where a sine would be too regular.

A slowly wandering pan position.

```tine
seed 6
voice spark = [^5 . ^8 . ^9 . . .].inst(bell).vel(.4).pan(drift(.25).range(-.8, .8))
```

Drift on how much a texture is thinned, so it breathes unpredictably.

```tine
seed 6
voice texture = [hat*16].degrade(drift(.5)).vel(.4)
```

A tiny pitch drift, like an old tape machine.

```tine
seed 6
voice keys = [c4@maj7 . . . a3@m7 . . .].inst(keys).transpose(drift(.5).range(-.2, .2))
```

See also: [noise](#noise), [sine](#sine), [walk](#walk).

### range

`range(signal, lo, hi)`: Rescale a 0..1 signal or pattern to lo..hi.

`range(lo, hi)` rescales a signal or a pattern of numbers from 0..1 to lo..hi. Almost every signal is used through it.

A sine from 400 to 3400 Hz on a low-pass filter.

```tine
voice pad = <c3@m9 f3@m9>.inst(pad).lpf(sine(8).range(400, 3400))
```

It works on a phrase of numbers too. Here 0..1 becomes velocities between .3 and .9.

```tine
voice hats = [hat*8].vel([0 .5 1 .5].range(.3, .9))
```

A range can run downwards: lo bigger than hi turns the signal over.

```tine
voice snare = [snare*16].vel(saw(1).range(1, .1))
```

See also: [sine](#sine), [seg](#seg), [lerp](#lerp).

### seg

`seg(signal, n)`: Sample a signal n times per bar, turning it into discrete events.

`seg(n)` samples a signal n times per bar, turning it into n separate events. That is how a smooth signal becomes notes.

A sine sampled 16 times, scaled to MIDI note numbers and rounded to whole notes. Numbers in a voice play as MIDI notes.

```tine
voice wave = sine(1).seg(16).range(60, 72).map(x => round(x)).inst(pluck)
```

Sample a slow drift once per beat to get a walking line in scale steps.

```tine
seed 3
voice line = drift(1).seg(4).range(0, 7).map(x => floor(x)).degrees.inst(keys)
```

See also: [sine](#sine), [range](#range), [as_cc](#as_cc).

### run

`run(n)`: The phrase [0 1 2 ... n-1].

`run(n)` is the phrase `[0 1 2 ... n-1]`. Combined with [`degrees`](#degrees) it is a scale; with [`map`](#map) it is anything you can compute from a counter.

Eight steps of the scale, from the tonic up.

```tine
key d dorian
voice scale = run(8).degrees.inst(pluck)
```

Every other step, by mapping the numbers, for a line in thirds.

```tine
voice thirds = run(8).map(i => i * 2).degrees.inst(keys)
```

A run as MIDI numbers: a chromatic climb from middle C.

```tine
voice chrom = run(12).map(i => 60 + i).inst(bell)
```

See also: [degrees](#degrees), [map](#map).

## Lists

### len

`len(list)`: Number of elements.

`len(list)` is the number of elements in a list, or of characters in a text.

Count the notes in a phrase.

```tine
let tune = [c4 e4 g4 b4 d5]
print(len(tune))
voice lead = tune.inst(pluck)
```

Use the length to fit a phrase to a grid: here it plays at one note per eighth, whatever its length, with [`poly`](#poly).

```tine
let tune = [c4 e4 g4 b4 d5]
voice lead = tune.poly(8).inst(pluck)
print(len(tune), "notes against 8 steps")
```

See also: [at](#at), [poly](#poly).

### at

`at(list, i)`: Element i (0-based; wraps around, so negative counts from the end).

`at(list, i)` is the element at position i, counting from 0. It wraps round, so -1 is the last element and any whole number is safe.

Pick one note from a list.

```tine
let scale = [c4 d4 e4 g4 a4]
voice tone = [(at(scale, 2)) (at(scale, -1))].inst(bell)
```

With [`per_bar`](#per_bar), step through a list one element per bar. Wrapping means the list just repeats.

```tine
let roots = [c2 f2 g2 c2 a1]
voice bass = per_bar(n => [(at(roots, n)) . (at(roots, n)) .]).inst(bass)
```

Index with arithmetic to walk a list in a pattern: every third element.

```tine
let scale = [^1 ^2 ^3 ^4 ^5 ^6 ^7]
voice line = run(8).map(i => at(scale, i * 3)).inst(pluck)
```

See also: [len](#len), [pick](#pick).

### map

`map(p, f)`: Apply f to every element of a list, or every event of a pattern.

`map(f)` applies a function to every element of a list, or to every note of a pattern. The rhythm stays; only the values change.

Add a fifth above every note, making each note a dyad.

```tine
voice fifths = [c4 d4 e4 g4].map(n => {(n) (n + 7)}).inst(organ)
```

Map numbers to notes. Here a list of intervals becomes pitches above C.

```tine
voice line = [0 4 7 11 14].map(i => pitch(60 + i)).inst(pluck)
```

Map a chord symbol onto each degree of a line, for parallel chords.

```tine
voice planing = [^1 ^2 ^3 ^5].map(deg => chord(deg, "7")).inst(keys)
```

See also: [filter](#filter), [fold](#fold), [run](#run).

### filter

`filter(list, f)`: Keep elements (or events) for which f is true.

`filter(f)` keeps the elements, or notes, for which the function is true. The rest are dropped (in a pattern they become rests).

Keep only the notes above middle C.

```tine
voice high = [c3 g3 c4 e4 g4 c5].filter(n => n > c4).inst(bell)
```

Keep the even numbers of a run, then play them as scale steps.

```tine
voice evens = run(12).filter(i => i % 2 == 0).degrees.inst(pluck)
```

Filter a random line to its chord tones.

```tine
seed 2
voice tones = dice([c4 d4 e4 f4 g4 a4 b4], 8).filter(n => n == c4 or n == e4 or n == g4).inst(keys)
```

See also: [map](#map), [degrade](#degrade).

### fold

`fold(list, start, f)`: Combine elements left to right: fold([1 2 3], 0, (a, x) => a + x).

`fold(list, start, f)` combines the elements one by one, left to right. Each step gets what has been built so far and the next element. Sums, running totals and built-up chords are all folds.

Add up a list of numbers.

```tine
print(fold([1 2 3 4], 0, (total, x) => total + x))
voice tone = [c4]
```

Stack intervals into a chord: start from a note, and each interval adds a note above the last.

```tine
let steps = [4 3 4 3]
let top = fold(steps, c4, (n, i) => n + i)
print(top)
voice keys = {c4 e4 g4 b4 (top)}.inst(keys)
```

See also: [sum](#sum), [map](#map).

### concat

`concat(a, b, ...)`: Join lists into one longer list (one bar, more steps).

`concat(a, b, ...)` joins lists into one longer list. As a phrase, it fits all the steps into one bar.

Two four-note figures joined into one eight-note bar.

```tine
voice arp = concat([c4 e4 g4 c5], [b4 g4 e4 b3]).inst(pluck)
```

Build a line from a list and a transformed copy of it.

```tine
let up = [^1 ^2 ^3 ^5]
voice line = concat(up, up.rev, up.step(2)).inst(keys)
```

See also: [seq](#seq), [repeat](#repeat).

### repeat

`repeat(x, n)`: A list of n copies of x.

`repeat(x, n)` is a list of n copies of x.

Sixteen hats in one bar.

```tine
voice hats = repeat(hat, 16).vel(.5)
```

Joined with other lists, for a riff with a repeated note.

```tine
voice riff = concat(repeat(c3, 5), [eb3 g3 bb3]).inst(bass)
```

See also: [concat](#concat), [ply](#ply).

### take

`take(list, n)`: The first n elements.

`take(list, n)` keeps the first n elements.

The first five notes of a scale.

```tine
voice five = take([c4 d4 e4 f4 g4 a4 b4 c5], 5).inst(pluck)
```

A phrase that grows by one note each bar.

```tine
let tune = [^1 ^3 ^5 ^4 ^3 ^2 ^1 ^7]
voice grow = per_bar(n => take(tune, n % 8 + 1)).inst(keys)
```

See also: [drop](#drop), [trunc](#trunc).

### drop

`drop(list, n)`: All but the first n elements.

`drop(list, n)` keeps everything after the first n elements.

A scale without its first three notes.

```tine
voice top = drop([c4 d4 e4 f4 g4 a4 b4 c5], 3).inst(pluck)
```

A phrase that shrinks from the front each bar.

```tine
let tune = [^1 ^3 ^5 ^4 ^3 ^2 ^1 ^7]
voice shrink = per_bar(n => drop(tune, n % 7)).inst(keys)
```

See also: [take](#take), [rotate](#rotate).

### rotate

`rotate(p, n)`: Start a list or rhythm n steps later in itself, wrapping round: [a b c d].rotate(1) is [b c d a]. A phrase with held or weighted steps, or a .beats line, turns by steps of its grid.

`rotate(n)` starts a list or a rhythm n steps later in itself, wrapping round: `[a b c d].rotate(1)` is `[b c d a]`. On rhythms with held or weighted steps, or a [`.beats`](#beats) line, it turns by steps of the rhythm's grid.

A melody, then the same melody started from its second note.

```tine
let tune = [c4 e4 g4 b4]
voice a = cat(tune, tune.rotate(1)).inst(pluck)
```

Rotate a rhythm to move its accents: the clave turned by three steps every fourth bar.

```tine
let clave = [X . . x . . X . . . x . X . . .]
voice turn = [^1 ^3 ^5 ^4 ^3 ^2 ^1].on(clave.every(4, r => r.rotate(3))).inst(keys)
```

A negative number rotates the other way.

```tine
voice line = [^1 ^2 ^3 ^4 ^5].rotate(-1).inst(bell)
```

See also: [iter](#iter), [displace](#displace), [on](#on).

### sum

`sum(list)`: Add up the elements.

`sum(list)` adds up the elements.

Add up beat lengths to check a [`.beats`](#beats) line is the length you meant.

```tine
print(sum([3/2 1/2 2 3 1/2 1/2 4]), "beats")
voice tune = [c4:3/2 d4:1/2 e4:2 a4:3 g4:1/2 f4:1/2 e4:4].beats.inst(keys)
```

A total used as a transposition: the sum of a few intervals.

```tine
voice tune = [c4 e4 g4].transpose(sum([2 2 1])).inst(pluck)
```

See also: [fold](#fold), [len](#len).

## Math

### floor

`floor(x)`: Round down.

`floor(x)` rounds down to a whole number. It works on numbers and on patterns of numbers.

Turn a smooth signal into whole scale steps.

```tine
voice steps = sine(1).seg(8).range(0, 7).floor.degrees.inst(pluck)
```

Print a few values.

```tine
print(floor(2.7), floor(-2.7))
voice tone = [c4]
```

See also: [ceil](#ceil), [round](#round).

### ceil

`ceil(x)`: Round up.

`ceil(x)` rounds up to a whole number.

Print a few values.

```tine
print(ceil(2.1), ceil(-2.1))
voice tone = [c4]
```

How many bars a line of beats needs: the total, divided by four and rounded up.

```tine
let lengths = [3 1 2 3 3]
print(ceil(sum(lengths) / 4), "bars")
voice tune = [c4:3 d4 e4:2 g4:3 e4:3].beats.inst(keys)
```

See also: [floor](#floor), [round](#round).

### round

`round(x)`: Round to nearest.

`round(x)` rounds to the nearest whole number. Use it to snap computed values to notes or steps.

Snap a sine to whole MIDI notes.

```tine
voice wave = sine(1).seg(16).range(60, 72).round.inst(pluck)
```

Snap a random walk in microtones to the nearest semitone, alongside the unsnapped version.

```tine
seed 3
voice micro = drift(2).seg(8).range(60, 67).inst(sine).pan(-.7)
voice snap  = drift(2).seg(8).range(60, 67).round.inst(sine).pan(.7)
```

See also: [floor](#floor), [ceil](#ceil).

### abs

`abs(x)`: Absolute value.

`abs(x)` is the size of a number without its sign.

Print a few values.

```tine
print(abs(-3), abs(3))
voice tone = [c4]
```

Fold a line around a centre: notes that would go below it are reflected above.

```tine
voice v = [-4 -2 0 2 4 2 0 -2].map(x => abs(x)).degrees.inst(pluck)
```

See also: [min](#min), [max](#max).

### sqrt

`sqrt(x)`: Square root.

`sqrt(x)` is the square root.

A curve that rises fast and then levels off, used for velocities.

```tine
voice beat = [hat*8].vel(run(8).map(i => sqrt(i / 7)).range(.2, .9))
```

Print a value.

```tine
print(sqrt(2))
voice tone = [c4]
```

See also: [exp](#exp), [log2](#log2).

### sin

`sin(x)`: Sine (radians).

`sin(x)` is the sine of an angle in radians. For a moving signal in time, use [`sine`](#sine) instead; `sin` is for computing values.

A line shaped by a sine, computed from a run of numbers.

```tine
voice wave = run(16).map(i => round(sin(i / 16 * 6.283) * 5)).degrees.inst(pluck)
```

Print a few values.

```tine
print(sin(0), sin(1.5708))
voice tone = [c4]
```

See also: [cos](#cos), [sine](#sine).

### cos

`cos(x)`: Cosine (radians).

`cos(x)` is the cosine of an angle in radians.

Two lines from sine and cosine: they move a quarter turn apart.

```tine
voice a = run(8).map(i => round(sin(i / 8 * 6.283) * 4)).degrees.inst(pluck)
voice b = run(8).map(i => round(cos(i / 8 * 6.283) * 4)).degrees.octave(-1).inst(bass)
```

Print a value.

```tine
print(cos(0))
voice tone = [c4]
```

See also: [sin](#sin).

### log2

`log2(x)`: Base-2 logarithm.

`log2(x)` is the base-2 logarithm. In music it turns a frequency ratio into octaves.

A frequency ratio in octaves, then in semitones (the same as [`ratio`](#ratio)).

```tine
print(log2(3/2), log2(3/2) * 12)
voice tone = [c4]
```

Notes from ratios: the harmonic series up from C2, each converted to semitones.

```tine
voice partials = run(8).map(k => c2 + log2(k + 1) * 12).inst(sine).vel(.4)
```

See also: [ratio](#ratio), [exp](#exp).

### exp

`exp(x)`: e to the power x.

`exp(x)` is e to the power x. It makes curves that start slow and speed up.

An exponential rise in velocity across a bar.

```tine
voice snare = [snare*16].vel(run(16).map(i => exp(i / 16 * 2) / exp(2)))
```

Print a value.

```tine
print(exp(1))
voice tone = [c4]
```

See also: [log2](#log2), [sqrt](#sqrt).

### min

`min(a, b, ...)`: Smallest value.

`min(a, b, ...)` is the smallest value. It works on pitches too.

Cap a computed note so a line never goes above a limit.

```tine
voice capped = run(12).map(i => min(c4 + i * 2, g4)).inst(pluck)
```

The lowest note of a few.

```tine
print(min(e4, c4, g4))
voice tone = [c4]
```

See also: [max](#max), [clamp](#clamp).

### max

`max(a, b, ...)`: Largest value.

`max(a, b, ...)` is the largest value.

Keep a falling line from going below a floor.

```tine
voice floor = run(12).map(i => max(c5 - i * 2, f4)).inst(pluck)
```

The highest note of a few.

```tine
print(max(e4, c4, g4))
voice tone = [c4]
```

See also: [min](#min), [clamp](#clamp).

### clamp

`clamp(x, lo, hi)`: Limit x to the range lo..hi.

`clamp(x, lo, hi)` keeps x between lo and hi.

A rising run of numbers, clamped: it waits at the bottom, climbs, then holds at the top.

```tine
voice line = run(12).map(i => clamp(i - 3, 0, 5)).degrees.inst(pluck)
```

Print a few values.

```tine
print(clamp(12, 0, 10), clamp(-1, 0, 10))
voice tone = [c4]
```

See also: [min](#min), [max](#max), [within](#within).

### lerp

`lerp(a, b, t)`: Linear blend from a to b.

`lerp(a, b, t)` blends from a to b: t = 0 gives a, t = 1 gives b, t = 0.5 halfway.

A gradual change over eight bars: each bar's cutoff is a blend between two values.

```tine
voice bass = per_bar(n => [c2 c2 c3 c2].inst(saw).cutoff(lerp(300, 3000, (n % 8) / 7)))
```

Print a value.

```tine
print(lerp(10, 20, .25))
voice tone = [c4]
```

See also: [range](#range).

## Misc

### print

`print(x, ...)`: Show values in the console.

`print(x, ...)` shows values in the console, and returns its first argument, so it can sit in the middle of a chain.

Print a few things to check them.

```tine
print("a4 is", hz(a4), "Hz, and here is a chord:", c4@maj7)
voice tone = [c4]
```

Because it passes its first argument on, it can go anywhere in an expression.

```tine
voice line = print([c4 e4 g4].rev).inst(pluck)
```

See also: [str](#str), [type](#type).

### str

`str(x)`: Text form of a value.

`str(x)` is the text form of a value. Use it to build messages or names.

Build a message from values.

```tine
let root = d4
print("the root is " + str(root))
voice tone = [(root)]
```

Show a chord the way Tine writes it.

```tine
print(str(c4@m7))
voice keys = [c4@m7].inst(keys)
```

See also: [print](#print), [type](#type).

### type

`type(x)`: The name of a value's type.

`type(x)` is the name of a value's type. It helps when a function complains about what it was given.

The types of a few values.

```tine
print(type(3), type(c4), type(^3), type([c e g]), type(c4@maj), type(sine(1)))
voice tone = [c4]
```

Use it to treat different kinds of values differently.

```tine
let up(x) = if type(x) == "number" then x + 1 else x
print(up(3), up(c4))
voice tone = [c4]
```

See also: [print](#print), [str](#str).

## Harmony

### changes

`changes(text, octave: 3)`: Chords from a lead sheet: changes("Dm7 G7 | Cmaj7 %"). Bars are split by |, chords in a bar share it, / holds a chord one more slot, % repeats the bar, N.C. is no chord. Loops over its bars.

`changes(text)` reads chords from a lead sheet. Bars are split by `|`, chords in one bar share it, `/` holds a chord one more slot, `%` repeats the bar and `N.C.` is no chord. It loops over its bars. The chords keep their names, so the sheet views can print them.

A ii-V-I, two bars, as written on a lead sheet.

```tine
voice keys = changes("Dm7 G7 | Cmaj7 | %").strum.inst(keys)
```

Two chords in a bar split it evenly. `/` lets one take more of the bar: here Am7 gets three beats and D7 one.

```tine
voice keys = changes("Cmaj7 | Am7 / / D7 | G7 | Cmaj7").inst(keys)
```

The changes are the start of a whole band: a bass from their roots, a comping part from their voicings.

```tine
let tune = changes("Am7 D7 | Gmaj7 Cmaj7 | F#m7b5 B7 | Em7 | %")
voice bass = tune.root.within(e1, e2).inst(upright)
voice comp = tune.rootless.voicelead.inst(keys).vel(.5)
```

See also: [chord](#chord), [root](#root), [voicelead](#voicelead), [rootless](#rootless).

### root

`root(p)`: The root of each chord (from its symbol, or named from its notes). Single notes pass through. Try changes(...).root.octave(-1) for a bass line.

`root` gives the root of each chord: from its symbol if it has one, otherwise named from its notes. Single notes pass through. It is the quickest bass line.

The roots of a progression, two octaves down.

```tine
voice bass = changes("Dm7 G7 | Cmaj7 A7").root.octave(-1).inst(bass)
```

A chord without a symbol is named from its notes. `{e4 g4 c5}` is C in first inversion, so its root is C.

```tine
voice keys = [{e4 g4 c5} {f4 a4 d5}].inst(keys)
voice bass = [{e4 g4 c5} {f4 a4 d5}].root.octave(-2).inst(bass)
```

Roots in a rhythm: put them on the hits of a bass rhythm with [`on`](#on).

```tine
let tune = changes("Cm7 | Fm7 | G7 | Cm7")
voice bass = tune.root.notes(bars: 4).on([x . . x . . x .]).octave(-1).inst(bass)
```

See also: [bassnote](#bassnote), [within](#within), [name](#name).

### bassnote

`bassnote(p)`: The bass note of each chord: the slash note of c@7/e, otherwise the root.

`bassnote` gives the bass note of each chord: the slash note of `c@7/e`, otherwise the root. Slash chords on a lead sheet make the bass move by step; this follows them.

A descending bass line written as slash chords.

```tine
voice bass = changes("C | C/B | Am | Am/G").bassnote.octave(-1).inst(bass)
```

Compare: [`root`](#root) stays on C, `bassnote` follows the slash.

```tine
let tune = changes("C C/E | F G/B")
voice roots = tune.root.octave(-1).inst(bass)
voice basses = tune.bassnote.octave(-2).inst(bass).vel(.6)
```

See also: [root](#root), [within](#within).

### tones

`tones(chord)`: A chord's notes as a list, low to high.

`tones(chord)` gives a chord's notes as a list, low to high. Once a chord is a list, every list function works on it.

Print the notes of a chord symbol.

```tine
print(tones(g3@7b9))
voice keys = [g3@7b9].inst(keys)
```

Play the notes of a chord as a melody, in a new order each bar.

```tine
seed 3
voice tune = tones(c4@maj9).scramble.inst(pluck)
```

Take the top two notes of a chord for a light voicing.

```tine
voice keys = tones(d4@m9).drop(3).inst(keys)
```

See also: [arp](#arp), [chord](#chord).

### name

`name(x, bars: 1)`: Name a chord, or the chords of a pattern, as a chord symbol: name({e g c5}) is "C/E".

`name(x)` names a chord as a chord symbol. On a pattern it names the chords bar by bar; `bars:` says how many. It is a quick way to check what you wrote.

Name a chord from its notes.

```tine
print(name({e4 g4 c5}), name({c4 e4 g4 bb4 d5}))
voice keys = [{e4 g4 c5}]
```

Name what a pattern plays over several bars.

```tine
let prog = <^1@7 ^6@7 ^2@7 ^5@7>
print(name(prog, bars: 4))
voice keys = prog.inst(keys)
```

See also: [interval](#interval), [tones](#tones).

### shell

`shell(p)`: Shell voicings: root, third and seventh, the bebop pianist's left hand.

`shell` voices each chord as root, third and seventh: the bebop pianist's left hand. Three notes say what a chord is with nothing extra.

Shell voicings for a ii-V-I.

```tine
voice comp = changes("Dm7 G7 | Cmaj7 | %").shell.inst(keys)
```

Shells on a short, offbeat comping rhythm.

```tine
let tune = changes("Cm7 F7 | Bbmaj7 Ebmaj7")
voice comp = tune.shell.notes(bars: 2).on([. x . . . x x .]).inst(keys).legato(.4)
```

See also: [guide](#guide), [rootless](#rootless).

### guide

`guide(p)`: Guide tones: just the third and seventh of each chord. Add .voicelead to hear them move by step.

`guide` keeps just the third and seventh of each chord, the guide tones. They are the notes that move by step from one chord to the next; add [`voicelead`](#voicelead) to hear it.

Guide tones through a ii-V-I, voice-led so they move as little as possible.

```tine
voice guide = changes("Dm7 G7 | Cmaj7 | %").guide.voicelead.inst(keys)
```

Guide tones over a root bass: a complete, very lean harmony.

```tine
let tune = changes("Am7 D7 | Gmaj7 | %")
voice bass  = tune.root.within(e1, e2).inst(upright)
voice guide = tune.guide.voicelead.inst(keys).vel(.5)
```

See also: [shell](#shell), [voicelead](#voicelead).

### rootless

`rootless(p, form: "a")`: Rootless voicings: four notes without the root (3-5-7-9, dominants use the 13th for the 5th). Form "a" starts on the third, "b" on the seventh.

`rootless` voices each chord in four notes without the root, leaving the root to the bass. Form "a" starts on the third, form "b" on the seventh. These are the standard jazz piano voicings.

A form voicings for a ii-V-I.

```tine
voice comp = changes("Dm7 G7 | Cmaj7 | %").rootless.inst(keys)
```

Alternating forms keeps the hand in one place: "a" on the ii, "b" on the V.

```tine
voice comp = cat(changes("Dm7").rootless("a"), changes("G7").rootless("b")).inst(keys)
```

Rootless voicings with a bass line on the roots.

```tine
let tune = changes("Fm7 Bb7 | Ebmaj7 Abmaj7")
voice bass = tune.root.within(e1, e2).inst(upright)
voice comp = tune.rootless.voicelead.inst(keys).vel(.5)
```

See also: [shell](#shell), [voicelead](#voicelead), [drop2](#drop2).

### drop2

`drop2(p)`: Drop-2 voicings: close position, with the second voice from the top dropped an octave.

`drop2` takes a close chord and drops its second voice from the top an octave. The chord spreads out and sounds open, the guitarist's and arranger's favourite.

Close position, then drop 2, on the same chord.

```tine
voice keys = cat(c4@maj7, c4@maj7.drop2).inst(keys)
```

Drop-2 voicings through changes, voice-led.

```tine
voice comp = changes("Cmaj7 Am7 | Dm7 G7").voicelead.drop2.inst(keys)
```

See also: [drop3](#drop3), [drop24](#drop24), [invert](#invert).

### drop3

`drop3(p)`: Drop-3 voicings: close position, with the third voice from the top dropped an octave.

`drop3` drops the third voice from the top an octave. The spread is wider than drop 2, with a gap in the middle.

Close, drop 2 and drop 3 on one chord.

```tine
voice keys = cat(c4@maj7, c4@maj7.drop2, c4@maj7.drop3).inst(keys)
```

Drop 3 through a turnaround: a wide, guitar-like sound.

```tine
voice gtr = changes("Cmaj7 A7 | Dm7 G7").voicelead.drop3.strum(1/64).inst(pluck)
```

See also: [drop2](#drop2), [drop24](#drop24).

### drop24

`drop24(p)`: Drop-2-and-4 voicings: the second and fourth voices from the top dropped an octave.

`drop24` drops the second and fourth voices from the top an octave. It is the widest of the drop voicings.

Drop 2 and 4 on a seventh chord.

```tine
voice keys = cat(c4@maj7, c4@maj7.drop24).inst(keys)
```

Drop 2 and 4 for a slow pad.

```tine
voice pad = changes("Fmaj7 | Em7 | Dm7 | Cmaj7").drop24.inst(pad)
```

See also: [drop2](#drop2), [drop3](#drop3).

### voicelead

`voicelead(p, around: e4)`: Voice leading: play each chord in the close-position inversion that moves least from the previous chord, staying near `around`. Deterministic: built on evolve, so the chain is replayed from bar 0.

`voicelead` plays each chord in the inversion that moves least from the chord before, near the note given by `around`. Chords then move smoothly, with common tones held. It is computed from bar 0, so jumping to any bar gives the same voicing.

Root-position chords jump. Voice-led, they move by step.

```tine
let prog = <c4@maj7 a3@m7 d4@m7 g3@7>
voice jumpy  = prog.inst(keys).pan(-.6)
voice smooth = prog.voicelead.inst(keys).pan(.6)
```

`around` sets the register the voicings stay near.

```tine
voice low  = changes("Dm7 G7 | Cmaj7 | %").voicelead(around: c4).inst(keys)
voice high = changes("Dm7 G7 | Cmaj7 | %").voicelead(around: c5).inst(bell).vel(.4)
```

Voice-led chords arpeggiated: each chord's line flows into the next.

```tine
voice arp = changes("Am | F | C | G").voicelead.arp("updown").fast(2).inst(pluck)
```

See also: [guide](#guide), [invert](#invert), [evolve](#evolve).

### interval

`interval(a, b, long: false)`: The interval between two pitches by size: interval(c4, e4) is "M3"; with long: true, "major 3rd". Tine counts semitones, so C-F# and C-Gb are both TT (tritone).

`interval(a, b)` names the interval between two pitches by size: `interval(c4, e4)` is "M3". With `long: true` it spells it out. Tine counts semitones, so C to F# and C to Gb are both a tritone.

Short and long names.

```tine
print(interval(c4, g4), interval(c4, g4, long: true), interval(e4, c5))
voice keys = [{c4 g4} {e4 c5}]
```

Compute an interval inside the piece and print it while building a part.

```tine
let low = c4
let top = low + 10
print(interval(low, top, long: true))
voice pair = {(low) (top)}.inst(keys)
```

See also: [name](#name), [ratio](#ratio).
